Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement here — attaching our standard PO template for your finance team to validate. A few constraints on our side that will determine approval and applicable pricing:

- Net terms: our default is Net45.
- Invoice cadence: we can accept either weekly invoices (for usage-billed services) or a consolidated monthly invoice (preferred). If weekly, we require a PO number on each invoice and a weekly statement reconciliation.
- PO metadata: invoice must include PO#, GL code, BU code, cost center, and ETA of service period.
- Discounting: any transactional/volume discounts must be documented in the SOW/Order Form and cannot be applied retroactively.

Two quick clarifying questions:
1) Can Redwood accept Net45 and provide consolidated monthly statements by default?
2) If we move to Net30, is there an early-payment discount available (your sales suggested a short-term 1–2% band)?

Appended: ProcureCo_PO_Template.xlsx (attached). Please confirm which combination (net terms + invoice cadence) will preserve the published Enterprise pricing band and whether you can provide an explicit conditional discount schedule we can route through our AP team.

Appreciate a response by EOD Monday — procurement needs this to finalize the PO.

Best,

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear list and the PO template.

Short answers up front: we can comply with the PO metadata fields and put PO# on every invoice. We can also generate either weekly or consolidated monthly invoices, but the discount profile changes depending on net terms and invoice cadence.

Notes / counterproposal:
- Option A (preferred for Redwood): Net30 payment terms + consolidated monthly invoice. Offer: 2.0% early-payment discount (if paid by Net15), or standard pricing otherwise. Monthly consolidation reduces AP overhead and supports simpler reconciliation for both sides.
- Option B: Net45 payment terms + consolidated monthly invoice. Offer: 1.0% conditional discount if ProcureCo signs a 12-month commitment and agrees to a monthly statement reconciliation process.
- Option C: Weekly invoices (as you suggested) — we can do this but require a small administrative surcharge (0.5% of monthly invoice volume) to cover increased settlement overhead; discount levels are lower in this route (0.5% conditional).

Im attaching our current pricing slab for the Enterprise Standard tier so finance can see the delta by option.

Questions for you:
- Is your AP team able to accept a monthly statement that aggregates weekly invoice lines (i.e., weekly lines visible but payment made once monthly)? That would let us offer Option B without the surcharge.
- Are GL / BU / cost center codes individually required on each invoice line or is header-level mapping acceptable?

Ill loop in finance and growth to make sure we can formalize the conditional discount and produce a DocuSign-ready order form.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Director, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

Mina — finance OK on conditional promo but with constraints:

- We can offer a promotional 2% early-pay discount for the first 3 billing cycles only (not 6) and limited to recurring usage charges. One-time fees and onboarding are excluded. If they want it extended to 6 months, we need a contractual commitment to a minimum monthly commitment (MMR) or a revenue protection clause.
- For Net45 we can offer 1% conditional discount, contingent on 12-mo commitment and acceptance of consolidated monthly statements (no weekly billing).
- Weekly invoices: wed need to add a 0.5% operational surcharge unless they integrate to our billing API (integration takes ~4 weeks).

Recommend we present Option A (Net30 + 2% early-pay for first 3 cycles) as the commercial sweet spot and Option B (Net45 + 1% conditional + no surcharge) as fallback.

+1 on excluding GL-level line requirements — header-level fields are fine as long as their ERP can map by invoice line in the monthly statement.

- Priyom
